facts.text: West Bay Shore began as part of the Secatogue Purchase in 1692, evolving from a quiet farming and fishing community into a residential hamlet in the 20th century.
Sagtikos Manor, built in the late 1600s, is one of Long Island’s oldest homes and served as a British headquarters during the American Revolution.
George Washington stopped at Sagtikos Manor during his 1790 tour of Long Island, making the hamlet a brief waypoint for the first U.S. president.
The manor’s historic significance earned it a place on the National Register of Historic Places in 1976, preserving more than three centuries of local history.
West Bay Shore’s waterfront homes line the shore, offering residents private docks and a direct connection to the Long Island Sound.
A Long Island Rail Road ride from Penn Station to the nearest station, followed by a short taxi or bus trip, brings you to West Bay Shore.
